history.dynasty: Present structure by Maratha Shridhar Bhonsle, 18th century
history.period: Origins traced to the 10th century CE (verify); present structure 18th century
history.summary: Nagvasuki Mandir at Daraganj on the Ganga bank is dedicated to Vasuki, king of serpents, who served as the churning rope in the Samudra Manthan. Legend says the wounded Vasuki was told by Vishnu to bathe at Triveni Sangam and rest, and he settled at this spot in Prayag; the Padma Purana is cited for Vasuki residing at Prayag (verify). The present structure was built by the Maratha king Shridhar Bhonsle in the 18th century after a royal priest's vow cured the king's serious illness, and he also built a ghat nearby. It is one of the few temples in India where Kaal Sarp Dosh remedial rituals are performed. Local legend says Aurangzeb's men could not destroy the temple (verify). A five-hooded stone Vasuki sits in the Vesara-style sanctum; a large reclining Bhishmapitamaha idol stands near the entrance. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is said to have stayed here three days on his first Prayag visit (verify). CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Allahabad' is approximate - the temple is at Daraganj, Prayagraj (city renamed Prayagraj in 2018); documented as Prayagraj.

name: Nagvasuki Mandir
town_description: Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) is the sacred city at the Triveni Sangam - the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and mythical Saraswati - and the site of the Kumbh and Magh Melas. It is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre as well as a historic city with the Mughal-era Allahabad Fort, Anand Bhavan and Prayagraj University.

travel.road: Nag Basuki Road, Daraganj, on the northern bank of the Ganga, north of the railway bridge; ~5 km from Triveni Sangam; reachable via congested bylanes or the newer shoreline route; auto/taxi
